title: Can You Install Carpet Over Radiant Floor Heat?
meta: Yes, carpet works over radiant floor heat if carpet and pad stay low in combined R-value and the pad is thin and dense. Edmonds rules from Wills Flooring.
keywords: carpet over radiant floor heat, best carpet pad for radiant heat, carpet R-value radiant heating, can you put carpet over heated floors, carpet installation Edmonds WA

blocks.lead: Yes, you can install carpet over radiant floor heat, as long as the carpet and pad together stay under the R-value your system was designed for, usually a combined total of about 2.5 or less, and you use a thin, dense pad instead of a thick foam one.
blocks.detail: Carpet is an insulator, which is exactly what a heated floor does not want. The fix is a dense, low-pile carpet and a pad made for radiant systems so heat still reaches the room. Wills Flooring installs carpet over hydronic and electric radiant floors across Edmonds at the published $0.99 per sq ft stretch-in rate and checks both layers against your system specs at the free estimate.

blocks.html: Radiant heat shows up in more Edmonds remodels every year: hydronic in the slab or stapled under the subfloor in Bowl and Seaview remodels, electric mats in Perrinville and Westgate additions. Tile in the bathroom is an easy call. The question comes in the bedrooms, where the owner wants warm floors and a soft surface at once. It gets done badly when the carpet is picked first and the pad last. Here is what to pick, in what order, and where carpet over radiant does not make sense.

blocks.text: Why the pad matters more than the carpet

items.title: R-value is the whole story
items.text: Every layer over a radiant tube or cable resists heat flow. Carpet and pad each have an R-value and they add up. Most systems are designed for a combined total in the low twos; above that the floor has to run hotter than the system can manage.

items.title: Pad is the bigger number
items.text: A thick prime foam pad can carry more R-value than the carpet on top of it. A thin, dense rubber, felt or radiant-rated rebond carries a fraction of that. Swap only the pad and you cut the assembly's resistance nearly in half.

items.title: Dense, low pile conducts best
items.text: Tall, airy plush traps air, and trapped air is insulation. A dense, low-pile cut or loop carpet lets heat through and wears better in bedrooms and halls. Wool feels warmer but runs slightly higher in R-value than nylon of the same build.

items.title: Output drops, comfort does not
items.text: A carpeted radiant room delivers less heat per square foot than a tiled one, so it warms slower. But carpet feels warm at a lower surface temperature than tile, so the room feels comfortable sooner than the numbers suggest.

blocks.text: Which radiant systems pair well with carpet

a.title: Carpet works when
items: Hydronic tubing stapled under the subfloor, which is common in Edmonds remodels
Hydronic in a slab, with a low-R carpet and pad assembly
A system sized with margin for a carpeted zone from the start
Bedrooms and living areas where a lower surface temperature is fine

b.title: Think twice when
items: Thin electric mats designed for tile that are not rated for carpet
A system sized for bare tile with no capacity to spare
You want a deep plush and a thick pad and are not willing to trade one
Rooms that rely on radiant as the only heat and need fast warm-up

blocks.text: Mistakes that turn warm floors lukewarm

items: Choosing the carpet first and letting the installer default to the thickest pad in the truck. The pad decides whether heat gets through.
Ignoring the system manual. Most manufacturers publish a maximum floor covering R-value and a maximum surface temperature. Exceeding either can void the system warranty.
Reusing the old thick pad because it looked fine. It was probably chosen for a room that never had heat under it.
Nailing tack strip over an electric mat without locating the cable. One staple through a cable means a dead zone or a repair through the new carpet.
Cranking the thermostat up the day after installation. Rapid heating stresses seams and adhesive before they have settled.
Expecting tile-level heat output. Carpeted radiant rooms warm gently: comfortable in an Edmonds winter, but not hot underfoot.

blocks.title: Edmonds zoning tip:
blocks.text: Most Edmonds hydronic systems run several zones. If the bedrooms are carpeted and the bath is tile, ask your heating contractor to give the carpeted zone its own supply temperature so the tile does not run cold while the bedroom catches up. Read our post on how carpet padding works before choosing a pad.
What to ask before you order

items.html: What is the system's maximum floor covering R-value? It is in the manual or available from the installer. Without it you are guessing.
What is the R-value of this exact pad? Ask for the spec sheet, not a description. Radiant-rated pads print the number on the label.
What is the carpet's R-value and pile height? Lower pile and higher density are the target. Our carpet installation page covers the fiber and construction choices.
Where are the tubes or cables? Get the layout drawing before install day, or plan for the installer to locate them.
Who sets the system temperature afterward? Agree the ramp-up with your heating contractor so nobody blames the carpet or the boiler.
Does the carpet warranty allow radiant? Most do, with a surface temperature cap. We check the mill's radiant terms before ordering and back the install with a 1-year workmanship warranty.

faq.q: Does carpet block radiant floor heat?
faq.a: It reduces it rather than blocking it. Carpet and pad are insulators, so a carpeted radiant room gets less heat per square foot than a tiled one. Keep the combined R-value around 2.5 or lower, with a thin dense pad, and most systems still heat the room comfortably.

faq.q: What is the best carpet pad for radiant heat?
faq.a: A thin, dense pad with a low R-value, such as a 1/4 inch rubber, felt or radiant-rated rebond pad. Avoid thick prime foam, which can carry more resistance than the carpet itself. The pad's R-value should be printed on its spec sheet.

faq.q: What type of carpet is best over heated floors?
faq.a: A dense, low-pile carpet in nylon, triexta or a tight loop. Low pile traps less air, so more heat comes through, and dense construction wears better. Thick plush, frieze and shag hold too much air and are poor choices over radiant.

faq.q: Can you put carpet over electric radiant floor mats?
faq.a: Only if the mat is rated for carpet. Many thin electric mats are made for tile and stone, and their warranties exclude soft floor coverings. Check the maker's documentation first; if it allows carpet, the pad rules and cable mapping still apply.

faq.q: Will tack strip nails damage radiant tubing?
faq.a: They can if the tubing sits in the subfloor or right below it. With staple-up systems under the subfloor there is nothing to hit. Over a slab or over-subfloor panels we locate the runs first, then glue or short-pin the strip in a safe zone.

faq.q: How long after carpet installation can I turn the radiant heat back on?
faq.a: Immediately at a low setting, then raise it gradually over two or three days to normal. A slow ramp lets seams and adhesive settle, and the same approach applies whenever the system starts up each fall.
